Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Absolutely! Here's a simple breakdown of the main whiskey types we carry:
Bourbon — American whiskey made primarily from corn. It's typically sweeter and smoother, with notes of vanilla, caramel, and oak. Great for beginners!
Scotch — Whisky from Scotland (note the spelling without the 'e'). Can range from light and smooth to rich and smoky. Blended Scotch (like Johnnie Walker) is easier to start with than single malts.
Rye — Spicier and bolder than bourbon, with peppery notes. More assertive flavor profile.
Irish Whiskey — Smooth and approachable, often triple-distilled. Light and easy-drinking.
Other Spirits — We also carry tequila, rum, vodka, and gin if you're interested in exploring beyond whiskey.
If you're completely new, I'd recommend starting with bourbon or blended Scotch — they're the most approachable. We also have a Whiskey Academy that combines guided video lessons with tasting samples, so you can learn while you taste.

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Great question! Here's your simple first-time tasting guide:
1. Pour the right amount
Pour about "two fingers" (1.5-2 ounces) into your glass — that's the height of two fingers held against the glass. Don't need much for tasting — three quarters of an ounce is plenty.
2. Smell it first (The Aroma)
Gently bring the glass to your nose — don't rush! You don't want to overwhelm your senses. Take your nose away after each sniff, then repeat. Trust the first thing you smell (vanilla, caramel, oak). The other layers will reveal themselves with each sniff.
3. Take a small sip (The Palate)
Take a small sip and roll it over your tongue and around your mouth. Savor the flavors — are they sweet? Spicy? Woody? Notice the texture and intensity.
4. Notice the finish
After you swallow, pay attention to how long the taste lingers in your mouth. The best spirits have a long, enjoyable finish.
5. Add water (optional)
After your first taste, try adding a few drops of water — it opens up the flavors and takes the edge off the alcohol.
Pro tip: Repeat the process a few times. With each sip, you'll notice new flavors you missed before.
